name: Intxorta front & Elgeta memory centre
story: After the loss of most of Gipuzkoa in 1936, Basque and Republican battalions stabilised the front on the Intxorta heights above Elgeta. They held these trenches through the winter and resisted the first weeks of Mola's spring 1937 offensive, until the line had to be abandoned in late April 1937 as the front collapsed towards Durango and Bilbao. Intxorta became a symbol of Basque resistance. The Basque Centre for the Interpretation of Historical Memory in Elgeta explains the fighting and the recovery of memory, and a signposted route leads to restored trenches, shelters and the 'Intxortako Atea' monument.
see: An interpretation centre in the village and a 5.8 km waymarked loop with restored trenches, shelters, viewpoints, the Intxortako Atea monument and the Salvador hermitage.
plan: Guided walks (about 3.5 h) usually run on the first and last Sunday of the month from the Espaloia café-theatre at 10:00; book on 943 71 89 11. The 'Elgeta memoria' app supports self-guided visits.
